title: Head-to-head comparison of verifier designs in LLM-driven NetOps pipelines (repaired preregistration)
research_question: When integrated into an LLM-driven intent→configuration pipeline (open-source network OS images only), which verifier design—(A) Batfish-style reachability checks, (B) SMT/formal-methods verifier (Z3-based constraint check), or (C) lightweight syntactic+runtime validator—yields the highest operational safety (fewer harmful misconfigurations) measured by connectivity-preservation across diverse synthetic and open-source OS topologies?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H0: There is no difference in paired connectivity-preservation rate between each verifier-assisted pipeline and the single-pass LLM baseline.
H1: At least one verifier-assisted pipeline (A, B, or C) yields a statistically higher paired connectivity-preservation rate than the single-pass LLM baseline.
exploratory_questions: E1: How do repair-iteration counts and time-to-repair differ by verifier design?
E2: Which failure-mode categories (semantic mismatch, vendor-agnostic misrendering, verifier false-positive/negative) dominate per verifier?
E3: How sensitive are verifier advantages to small, pre-registered prompt perturbations?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic topologies (3–12 nodes) instantiated with open-source network OS images only (FRRouting/FRR, VyOS, Open vSwitch) executed in Docker-based emulation (public images).
Tasks: intent classes: routing (static/OSPF-like), ACL/policy, NAT, VLAN/isolation.
model_scope: Single hosted LLM API (one fixed version; exact model identifier recorded in execution manifest).
No proprietary vendor OS images; all emulation uses public images and recorded image hashes.
transformation_scope: Template -> CLI rendering for FRR, VyOS, OVS.
primary_estimand: Per-intent paired difference in connectivity-preservation (binary) between each verifier-assisted pipeline and the single-pass LLM baseline (unit = intent).
secondary_estimands: Distribution of repair iterations per intent (median, IQR).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample: N_confirmatory = 120 intents, stratified into 4 task clusters (routing, ACL, NAT, VLAN) with 30 intents per cluster. Discovery/prompt-sensitivity sample: N_discovery = 30 (held-out). Total intents executed = 150. Fixed random seeds and frozen prompt templates. For emulator/container failure an intent is requeued up to 2 automatic re-executions; if still failing the intent is replaced by the next pre-registered held-out intent until confirmatory N reached or compute budget exhausted. All replacements, failures, and hashes are logged.
power_and_precision_plan: Recommended scenario: N_confirmatory=120, N_discovery=30 (total 150). Primary estimand: paired connectivity-preservation difference. Target effect: absolute improvement ≈10 percentage points (e.g., 80%→90%). Family-wise alpha adjustment for three primary comparisons: Bonferroni alpha_adjusted=0.05/3=0.0167. Planned test: McNemar (two-sided) per pair; 95% Agresti–Coull CIs reported for paired differences. With N=120, adjusted-alpha McNemar planning yields power ≈0.80 for ~8–10 pp differences under conservative discordant assumptions; exact MDEs recomputed and reported alongside results. Sensitivity: recompute power under baseline rates 70% and 85%; bootstrap CIs for paired differences.
exclusion_rules: Exclude runs whose generated CLI contains disallowed external-fetch/remote-exec tokens (e.g., curl, wget, remote shell, embedded URLs) — deterministic token-matching.
Exclude runs where container/image hash != preregistered image hash.
Exclude runs where verifier returns malformed/unexpected structured outputs (schema error) or verifier runtime fails after retries.
Exclude intents that fail emulation/verifier after 2 automatic re-executions; replaced according to sampling_plan.
missingness_plan: Automatic retry policy: up to 2 automatic re-executions on emulator/container or verifier runtime failure. If still failing the intent is flagged, logged with timestamp/reason/hash, and replaced by next pre-registered held-out intent until confirmatory N reached or compute budget exhausted. Flagged/excluded items are removed from primary confirmatory analysis; sensitivity analyses: (a) treat flagged items as failures, (b) include flagged items (where safe) and report differences. All exclusions, replacements, and timestamps are recorded and reported.
analysis_plan: Primary outcome per intent: connectivity-preserved (yes/no) per condition. For each pre-specified pair (Verifier A vs baseline, Verifier B vs baseline, Verifier C vs baseline) perform McNemar two-sided test using adjusted alpha=0.0167. Report paired absolute differences with 95% Agresti–Coull CIs. For repair iterations and time: report median and IQR; compare with Wilcoxon signed-rank or paired bootstrap if distributional assumptions fail. Apply pre-specified failure-mode taxonomy to logs; report counts and representative examples. All analyses run deterministically with fixed seeds; raw CLI artifacts, logs, model calls, and verifier outputs retained and checksummed for audit.
multiplicity_plan: Primary family: three pre-specified comparisons (each verifier vs baseline) controlled via Bonferroni (alpha_adjusted=0.0167) for confirmatory claims. Secondary comparisons (verifier vs verifier) and exploratory subgroup analyses reported as exploratory; for interpretive context apply Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control but do not use for confirmatory conclusions.
contamination_plan: Risk factors: prompt-injection in inputs, tool-chain compromise, emulator image drift, hosted-LLM nondeterminism. Detection procedures: pre-run image-hash integrity checks; deterministic token-based LLM-output filtering for disallowed patterns; per-run prompt and model-call checksum logging; runtime verifier schema assertions. Item-flagging rules: automatic exclusion on disallowed tokens or image-hash mismatch; mark verifier-assertion-fail where verifier returns malformed outputs. Analysis treatment: flagged items excluded from primary confirmatory analysis and reported; sensitivity analyses include flagged-as-failure and flagged-removed results. All detection, flags, and remediation logged automatically; no human adjudication.
stopping_rule: Stop when confirmatory N (recommended: 120) is reached OR planned_model_calls budget exhausted OR 7-day wall-clock limit reached. Per-intent stopping: abort attempts for an intent after 2 automatic re-executions and replace per sampling_plan. Abort full run immediately on detected image-hash mismatch of a core emulation image (safety-critical contamination) until image integrity is restored; all such events are logged.
planned_outputs: Frozen preregistration document (this record) with hashes.
Execution manifest: model identifier, image hashes, prompt templates, seeds, run timestamps.
Raw artifacts: generated CLIs, rendered configurations, verifier inputs/outputs, emulator traces, repair logs.
Failure-analysis record and failure-mode taxonomy counts with examples.
Evidence-to-claim table and nearest-work comparison matrix.
Complete IEEE LaTeX manuscript (≤5 pages) and compiled PDF.
Autonomous revision log and methodological/statistical reviews.
Final-output hash manifest and reproducibility instructions.
